comparator.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme totals 180 ECTS. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 ECTS of mathematics, statistics, economics, econometrics, operations research, programming and development work. Year 3 contains a 30-ECTS mobility or elective window, 12 ECTS of philosophy and ethics, one 6-ECTS compulsory elective and a 12-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit GROW and software-workshop activities are excluded. The 30-ECTS mobility window and the 6-ECTS compulsory elective remain genuine choice space rather than being filled with assumed courses.
components: Open exchange, study-abroad or five-elective space.
Philosophy of Economics and Economic Ethics
One course chosen from the current official semester-one or semester-two compulsory-elective lists.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Statistics, econometrics, forecasting and empirical inference

How can data be used to estimate, forecast and support decisions under uncertainty?
How can quantitative methods improve policy, public services and nonprofit decisions?

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics, econometrics & optimisation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around economics, econometrics and optimisation, supported by mathematics, statistics, programming, algorithms and data analysis; the label avoids presenting UCR as offering the comparator's full specialist econometrics sequence.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible response to Tilburg Econometrics and Operations Research built around mathematics, statistics, econometrics, economics, programming, algorithms and optimisation.
progression: Programming, economics and corporate-finance foundations begin in Semester 1. Mathematical Methods, Research Methods and introductory data science precede the mathematics, statistics, econometrics and advanced data work. Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms; optimisation follows programming and the main mathematical foundations, while reinforcement learning is reserved for the final semester after programming and machine learning. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Econometrics, data science & predictive modelling
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains the econometric and economic core but adds software development, neural networks, AI ethics and AI/business applications, making data science and predictive modelling a visible organising strand rather than calling the whole programme simply Econometrics.
alternatives.concept: A business-analytics and data-science direction combining econometrics with programming, software development, machine learning, neural networks, algorithms and quantitative economic or public-value applications.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest-match curriculum, this route replaces accounting/corporate finance, public economics, numerical methods and general ethics with database management, software development, neural networks, AI ethics and explicit AI/business applications. Those changes make computational data science and predictive modelling, rather than the broad economics-and-operations-research core, the additional organising logic.
progression: Programming, introductory data science and economics begin in Semester 1. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods precede the advanced mathematics, neural networks and econometrics. Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms; software development, advanced algorithms, neural networks and the AI/business application course are placed in Year 2 after the foundations. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics & finance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines mathematical, statistical and econometric training with accounting, business foundations, banking and finance, macroeconomics and behavioural economics; this supports a finance direction without overstating UCR as offering a full specialist quantitative-finance major.
alternatives.concept: A quantitative-finance direction combining mathematics, statistics, econometrics and programming with corporate finance, banking, macroeconomics, microeconomics and financial decision-making.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest-match curriculum, the finance route adds business foundations, database management, Money, Banking & Finance and behavioural economics while dropping advanced algorithms, logic and discrete mathematics, optimisation and reinforcement learning. Those changes shift the curricular centre toward financial and economic decision-making. It differs still more clearly from the data-science route through its accounting, banking, public-economics and behavioural-economics content.
progression: Business foundations precede Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability, advanced calculus and numerical methods; Research Methods precedes the advanced economics and econometrics courses; programming precedes algorithms and computational decision-making. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Business analytics, data science and public-value modelling

selection.assessment: The closest curriculum supports broad quantitative economics, econometrics and optimisation. Business analytics/data science and quantitative finance each support coherent, mechanically feasible and substantively distinct additional programmes. Actuarial science was assessed separately but rejected because UCR lacks a sufficient dedicated insurance and life-contingencies sequence. Three alternatives are included, the maximum.

blocks: Both provide foundational mathematical techniques for later quantitative study; UCR is broader and includes calculus and linear algebra.
Both develop matrix methods, vector spaces and systems of linear equations.
Both develop calculus and multivariable analysis for quantitative modelling; the exact depth and sequence differ.
Both provide probability foundations; UCR also includes statistical inference and simulation.
Both provide statistical and empirical-analysis foundations; UCR is more applied and less mathematically specialised.
Both develop multivariate statistical analysis and inference; UCR teaches it in behavioural-science research rather than econometrics.
UCR does not reproduce Tilburg’s second dedicated mathematical-analysis course.
UCR has linear algebra but not Tilburg’s additional advanced linear-algebra course.
UCR does not reproduce this dedicated differentiation and integration theory course.
Both provide programming foundations for computational quantitative work.
Both develop optimisation methods under formal constraints; UCR spans a broader range of AI search and optimisation techniques.
Both model decisions under uncertainty and constraints; UCR uses a broader artificial-intelligence framing.
Both provide microeconomic foundations, although UCR also introduces macroeconomics in the same course.
Both develop macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, policy and international economic relationships.
Both analyse choice, equilibrium and strategic behaviour with formal economic models; Tilburg is explicitly mathematical.
Both develop regression-based econometric estimation, testing, causal analysis and prediction.
Both introduce financial decision-making; UCR covers accounting and corporate finance but not actuarial mathematics.
Both address financial markets, valuation, risk and investment decisions; UCR also includes banking and personal finance.
UCR has one later econometrics course but no separate introductory econometrics course in these schedules.
Both support reflective competence and professional development; UCR is a broader personal and professional development course.
Both provide structured ethical reasoning; UCR Ethics is general rather than economics-specific.
UCR develops academic communication across courses but has no dedicated EOR communication-skills component.
UCR courses include applied projects, but not Tilburg’s dedicated Improving Society Lab sequence.
The comparator’s open mobility or elective window is not filled with assumed courses.
UCR has philosophy and AI ethics, but no dedicated philosophy-of-science-and-statistics course.
The comparator’s choice among listed specialist electives remains open rather than assumed.
UCR’s optional independent-research element is shown separately and does not make the Tilburg thesis a direct course match.

notes.text: UCR does not reproduce Tilburg’s complete specialist sequence in mathematical analysis, advanced linear algebra, statistics for econometrics, actuarial mathematics or the required econometrics thesis; those gaps remain explicit rather than being filled by weak matches.
